```{r}
# Clean up the data
structured_data <- raw_data %>%
  # Filter out test responses and incomplete responses; the Feedback filters will save BOTH empty feedback AND feedback with text that does not say "Test"    
  filter(Finished == 1, Status == 0, toupper(Feedback) != "TEST" | is.na(Feedback) , !is.na(Age), !is.na(Agree_Condition), 
         !is.na(Mode_Condition), ID != 15, ID != 16, ID != 29, ID != 30, ID != 33, ID != 34, ID != 39, ID != 40, ID != 55, ID != 56, ID != 223, ID != 224, ID != 240, ID != 259, ID != 272, 
         ID != 279, ID != 280, ID != 285, ID != 286, ID != 287, ID != 288, ID != 313, ID != 314, ID != 293, ID != 294, ResponseId != "R_3O17e9W1LFepRoW") %>% # Excluding IDs for which the session didn't go properly (e.g. didn't actually disagree on the issue) (or for which a participant already took the full study before) (including some with condition mess-ups); also note that ID 276 didn't click the checkbox to change condition (as they were supposed to), but were verbally instructed about the change, so keeping in the data
  # Rename to get rid of the capital letters; also create new agreement condition column to put the actual condition into (save the Agree_Condition column with the original condition)
  mutate(mode_condition = Mode_Condition, 
         # Initialize column that will eventually have the CORRECT agreement condition (including the ones that were changed; keep the Agree_Condition variable with the original agreement condition)
         agree_condition = 0,
         orig_agree_condition = Agree_Condition,
         awkward_predict_reverse = 10 - awkward_predict,
         awkward_experience_reverse = 10 - awkward_experience,
         hostile_predict_reverse = 10 - hostile_predict,
         hostile_experience_reverse = 10 - hostile_experience,
         Topic = factor(Topic),
         topic_text = 0,
         topic_opinion_before = 0,
         true_partner_opinion_before = 0,
         true_partner_opinion_after = 0)

# Change ID number of one participant who accidentally got same link as participant of the other ID number (i.e. ID 273 appears twice, but one of them should be 274)
structured_data[structured_data$ResponseId == "R_3qHFQeh4VXUaA0v","ID"] <- 274

# Create variable with each P's opinion on the selected topic
for(i in seq_along(structured_data$topic_opinion_before)) {
  if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '1') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$abortion_opinion[i]  
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "abortion"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '2') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$samesex_opinion[i]  
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "same_sex"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '3') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$gun_opinion[i]  
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "gun_control"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '4') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$blm_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "blm"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '5') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$family_opinion[i]  
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "family_separation"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '6') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$climate_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "climate_change"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '7') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$god_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "god"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '8') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$restrict_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "religious_freedom"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '9') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$church_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "church_state"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '10') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$police_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "police"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '11') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$confederate_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "confederate"
  } else if(structured_data$Topic[i] == '12') {
    structured_data$topic_opinion_before[i] = structured_data$mask_opinion[i] 
      structured_data$topic_text[i] = "mask"
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Clean up log data
cleaned_log_data <- log_data %>%
  # Rename the variables with long names
  dplyr::rename(log_agree_condition = `Agreement Condition ("agree" or "disagree") (enter twice - one row for each participant)`,
                log_mode_condition = `Mode Condition ("monologue" or "dialogue")`,
                log_change_condition = `Did you change the Agreement condition? (Leave BLANK if no; if yes, simply enter the condition you changed it to - enter either "agree" or "disagree" exactly)`,
                ID = `Participant ID`,
                session_number = `Sesssion Number`,
                log_notes = `Enter notes here, e.g. did anything unusual happen while running this participant? Any reasons why the data might be invalid, etc.?`,
                log_notes2 = ...13,
                recording_length = `Length of Recording(s) from the Session in minutes (round to the nearest minute)`)

# Merge the log data with the main data file
full_data <- left_join(structured_data, cleaned_log_data, by = "ID") %>%
  # Create column to label any pairs where the topic of discussion was selected non-randomly (e.g. if spreadsheet wasn't working)
  mutate(non_random_topic = 0,
         non_random_mode = 0,
         non_random_condition = 0,
         wrong_instructions = 0,
         rev_score_oppose_opinion = 0,
         rev_score_oppose_other = 0) %>%
  arrange(session_number)

# Label the following sessions as having a non-random topic of discussion
non_random_topic_sessions <- c(16) # continue here
for(i in seq_along(non_random_topic_sessions)) {
  full_data[full_data$session_number == non_random_topic_sessions[i],"non_random_topic"] <- 1
}

# Change monologue/dialogue condition
change_mode_sessions <- c(37, 38) # continue here
for(i in seq_along(change_mode_sessions)) {
  full_data[full_data$session_number == change_mode_sessions[i],"non_random_mode"] <- 1
}


# Create column with the TRUE agreement condition (i.e. if changed), and fill in other column to indicate if agreement condition was changed (based on the RA's notes, rather than the participants' entries)
for(i in seq_along(full_data$agree_condition)) {
  if(!is.na(full_data$log_change_condition[i]) && full_data$log_change_condition[i] == "agree" 
     && full_data$orig_agree_condition[i] == "disagree") {
    full_data$agree_condition[i] = "agree" 
    } else if(!is.na(full_data$log_change_condition[i]) && full_data$log_change_condition[i] == "disagree" && full_data$orig_agree_condition[i] == "agree") {
    full_data$agree_condition[i] = "disagree"
    } else {
  full_data$agree_condition[i] = full_data$orig_agree_condition[i]
}
}

# Fill in column to indicate a "1" for non-random agreement condition assignment
for(i in seq_along(full_data$non_random_condition)) {
  if(full_data$orig_agree_condition[i] != full_data$agree_condition[i]) {
    full_data$non_random_condition[i] = 1
  } else {
    full_data$non_random_condition[i] = 0
  }
}

# Create column for participants who saw the wrong agree/disagree instructions (because they clicked the checkbox to change condition assignment in the survey even though the experimenter indicated that the condition did not change)
for(i in seq_along(full_data$wrong_instructions)) {
  if(full_data$non_random_condition[i] != 1 && full_data$change_agree_cond_1[i] == 1
     && !is.na(full_data$change_agree_cond_1[i])) {
    full_data$wrong_instructions[i] = 1
            } else {
    full_data$wrong_instructions[i] = 0
  }
}

# Create reverse-scored column for own attitides and predictions of others' atti
for(i in seq_along(full_data$rev_score_oppose_opinion)) {
  if(full_data$topic_opinion_before[i] < 0)  {
    full_data$rev_score_oppose_opinion[i] = 0 - full_data$topic_opinion_before[i]
    full_data$rev_score_oppose_other[i] = 0 - full_data$predict_attit_before[i]
            } else {
    full_data$rev_score_oppose_opinion[i] = full_data$topic_opinion_before[i]
    full_data$rev_score_oppose_other[i] = full_data$predict_attit_before[i]
  }
}


  # For main analyses, exclude the participants who saw the wrong instructions from the data frame, and also create the composite measures
full_data <- full_data %>%
  filter(wrong_instructions == 0) %>%
  mutate(agree_condition = factor(agree_condition),
         mode_condition = factor(mode_condition),
         composite_predict = (enjoy_predict + awkward_predict_reverse + learn_predict + 
                                hostile_predict_reverse) / 4,
         composite_experience = (enjoy_experience + awkward_experience_reverse + learn_experience + 
                                hostile_experience_reverse) / 4,
         humaniz_comp_predict = (intell_predict + thought_predict + rational_predict) / 3,
         humaniz_comp_experience = (intell_experience + thought_experience + rational_experience) / 3,
         absol_attit_change = abs(opinion_after - topic_opinion_before),
         # This gives how different people thought their partner's opinion was to their own (as initially reported) before the conversation:
         own_predicted_other_before = abs(predict_attit_before - topic_opinion_before),
         # This gives how different people thought their partner's opinion was to their own (as initially reported) after the conversation:
         own_predicted_other_after = abs(partner_attit_before - topic_opinion_before))
```

```{r}
# Create variables with partner's opinion on the selected topic before AND after interaction
for(i in seq_along(full_data$session_number)) {
  if(i < length(full_data$session_number) &&
     full_data$session_number[i] == full_data$session_number[i+1]) {
    full_data$true_partner_opinion_before[i] = full_data$topic_opinion_before[i+1]
    full_data$true_partner_opinion_after[i] = full_data$opinion_after[i+1]
  } else if(i > 1 && 
             full_data$session_number[i] == full_data$session_number[i-1]) {
    full_data$true_partner_opinion_before[i] = full_data$topic_opinion_before[i-1]
    full_data$true_partner_opinion_after[i] = full_data$opinion_after[i-1]
  } else {
    full_data$true_partner_opinion_before[i] = NA
    full_data$true_partner_opinion_after[i] = NA
  }
}

# Create new variables for attitude comparison
full_data <- full_data %>%
  mutate(own_before_other_before = abs(topic_opinion_before - true_partner_opinion_before),
         own_after_other_before = abs(opinion_after - true_partner_opinion_before),
         abs_change_toward_other = own_before_other_before - own_after_other_before,
         # abs_change_toward_other will tell whether each P's attitude got CLOSER to the other person's initial attitude (positive number), or FURTHER from the other person's initial attitude (negative number)
         predict_other_before_diff = abs(predict_attit_before - topic_opinion_before),
         predict_other_after_diff = abs(partner_attit_before - topic_opinion_before),
         change_other_prediction = predict_other_before_diff - predict_other_after_diff,
          # change_other_prediction should show whether people thought the other person's opinion was (originally) LESS different from the P's own (original) opinion AFTER the interaction than before (positive number), or MORE different from the P's own (original) opinion AFTER the interaction than before (negative number)
         predict_other_new_after_diff = abs(partner_attit_after - topic_opinion_before),
         own_after_other_after = abs(opinion_after - true_partner_opinion_after),
         expected_diff_after = abs(partner_attit_after - opinion_after),
         before_after_actual_diffs = own_after_other_after - own_before_other_before,
         # note that "before_after_actual_diffs," really only makes sense at the pair level, because there is only one difference in opinions per pair (i.e. it is the same difference for each participant within the pair)
         expected_actual_before = predict_other_before_diff - own_before_other_before,
         # this is the difference between expectations of the (absolute) difference in attitudes and the actual (absolute) difference in attitudes BEFORE
         expected_actual_after = expected_diff_after - own_after_other_after,
         # this is the difference between expectations of the (absolute) difference in attitudes and the actual (absolute) difference in attitudes AFTER
         abs_topic_opinion_before = abs(topic_opinion_before),
         abs_predict_attit_before = abs(predict_attit_before),
         abs_partner_attit_after = abs(partner_attit_after))
```



```{r}
# Create separate data frames for prediction and experience measures, in order to combine them into one data frame with two rows per participant (for each of their observations)
prediction_only <- full_data %>%
  dplyr::select(-false_experience:-rational_experience, -awkward_experience_reverse,
                -hostile_experience_reverse, -composite_experience, -own_predicted_other_after,
                -humaniz_comp_experience) %>%
  dplyr::rename(false = false_predict,
         similar = similar_predict,
         enjoy = enjoy_predict,
         awkward = awkward_predict,
         awkward_reverse = awkward_predict_reverse,
         learn = learn_predict,
         hostile = hostile_predict,
         hostile_reverse = hostile_predict_reverse,
         like = like_predict,
         partlike = partlike_predict,
         connect = connect_predict,
         intell = intell_predict,
         thought = thought_predict,
         rational = rational_predict,
         composite = composite_predict,
         humaniz_composite = humaniz_comp_predict,
         own_minus_predicted_other = own_predicted_other_before) %>%
  mutate(phase = "prediction",
         attitude_prediction_stage = "before")

experience_only <- full_data %>%
  dplyr::select(-false_predict:-rational_predict, -awkward_predict_reverse,
                -hostile_predict_reverse, -composite_predict, -own_predicted_other_before,
                -humaniz_comp_predict) %>%
  dplyr::rename(false = false_experience,
         similar = similar_experience,
         enjoy = enjoy_experience,
         awkward = awkward_experience,
         awkward_reverse = awkward_experience_reverse,
         learn = learn_experience,
         hostile = hostile_experience,
         hostile_reverse = hostile_experience_reverse,
         like = like_experience,
         partlike = partlike_experience,
         connect = connect_experience,
         intell = intell_experience,
         thought = thought_experience,
         rational = rational_experience,
         composite = composite_experience,
         humaniz_composite = humaniz_comp_experience,
         own_minus_predicted_other = own_predicted_other_after) %>%
  mutate(phase = "experience",
         attitude_prediction_stage = "after")

monologue_data <- bind_rows(prediction_only, experience_only) %>%
  mutate(phase = factor(phase,
                        levels = c("prediction", "experience")))

```

**DUE TO A PROGRAMMING ERROR IN THE SURVEY THAT MESSED UP THE MANIPULATION FOR THE MONOLOGUE-DISAGREEMENT CONDITION, WE WERE UNABLE TO ANALYZE THE MONOLOGUE CONDITIONS IN THIS STUDY. WE THEREFORE ONLY REPORT ANALYSES OF THE DIALOGUE CONDITIONS IN THE SUPPLEMENT. (WE RE-RAN THIS STUDY, CORRECTING THE ERROR, AND REPORT THAT AS EXPERIMENT 3 IN THE MAIN TEXT.)**

```{r}
monologue_data_dialogue_only <- monologue_data %>%
  filter(mode_condition == "dialogue")
```

**Composite**

```{r}
composite_dialogue <- lmer(composite ~ agree_condition  * phase + (1|session_number) +
                           (1|session_number:ID), data = monologue_data_dialogue_only)
anova(composite_dialogue)
effectsize::eta_squared(anova(composite_dialogue))
```

```{r}
# Means
monologue_data_dialogue_only %>%
  group_by(agree_condition, phase) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean = round(mean(composite),2),
                   se = round(std.error(composite),2))
```
